title: webhook.received.v1
description: A gateway webhook was received, signature-verified and persisted. Published by Webhook Ingestion (BC-7) on pp.webhooks.inbound.v1, keyed by gateway_ref. The ingress does nothing else: verify, deduplicate, persist, publish, return 202 inside a 50 ms budget. All interpretation happens asynchronously, because returning quickly is what stops a gateway's retry policy from amplifying an incident. This is the ONE place a foreign vocabulary is legal in a payload - gatewayEventType and body are the gateway's own shapes, because the anti-corruption layer has not run yet.

gatewayRef.description: The gateway's own event identifier. Both the deduplication key and the partition key, so all deliveries of one gateway event are ordered and land on one consumer.

gatewayEventType.description: The gateway's own type string, untranslated.

signatureValid.description: Always true. An invalid signature is rejected at ingress and never published - publishing an unverified webhook would put an attacker's payload on the same topic as a genuine one.

bodySha256.description: Digest of the exact bytes received, letting the processor re-verify against the stored body rather than trusting a re-encoded parse.

payloadRef.description: Object-storage URI, present when the body exceeds the 256 KiB envelope cap. In practice this is the only event type that approaches it.

body.description: The parsed body when it is under the cap, redacted through the same allowlist as logs. Absent when payloadRef is used.
